utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning to the technical booth and the interpreters; good morning to the OTP and the Defence counsel. Good morning, General Krstic. How are you today? Is everything all right today? Are you better? You may remain seated, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not feeling well, and they have -- the doctors have told me that my leg might have to be amputated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the doctors are considering that, are they?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we regret that profoundly. Please sit down, and we hope that you will be feeling better. Let us take up our work where we left off, and I know that we have come to the point of documents, but perhaps we can hear who the next witness is, and then we can see to the documents after that. We have a set of documents, but shall we allow the witness -- shall we hear about the witness first please. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, Mr. President, my learned colleagues of the Prosecution, and everybody else in the courtroom. The Defence for today has one more witness who will be testifying. The witness has asked for protective measures: voice, image, and name. He has asked for a pseudonym. Prior to this morning's proceedings, we talked to the Prosecutor, and he agrees with those requests. The Defence, in view of this agreement, will present the reasons for which it is requesting protective measures for this witness. First of all, the first reason is the environment in which he lives, his profession. He is a professional officer, and the possibility of working together with representatives, that is to say, the army of the other entity, and the continuous return of refugees from the area in which he lives, this, in his view, could have some negative implications because in his place of residence, which is a relatively small place, he is known by both sides. When I say "both sides," I mean both populations, both ethnic groups living in the locality. So those are the reasons for which the witness has requested protective measures, because he feels that there could be some adverse consequences if it be known that he has testified here. And he was an active participant in the events of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. Petrusic. I see the Prosecutor, it is Mr. McCloskey, on his feet. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Yes, we've spoken, and we concur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber, bearing in mind the reasons presented by the Defence, and in view of no opposition from the OTP, and taking into consideration the fact that there are reasons which justify protective measures to be accorded, the Chamber does indeed accord those protective measures so that the testimony of the witness will be conducted under those protective measures. May we have the blinds drawn, please, for a moment, and have the witness shown in, please. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before the witness comes into the courtroom, the Defence would like to propose to the Trial Chamber that we go into closed session for a moment because the witness will identify the unit he was in and which he commanded, and so the identification of that unit would lead to his own identification, which would mean that the protective measures would not serve their purpose. So that is my request. It won't last more than a few minutes while we get through the witness' particulars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Madam Registrar, what is the pseudonym accorded to this witness? DF?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's DF, and he is Defence Witness number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DF. It is I who am addressing you. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the usher. Would you please hand the solemn declaration to the witness for him to read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated, and try to sit as comfortably as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for coming, first of all. You are going to take a look at the piece of paper handed to you and tell us whether that is your name, with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Thank you very much. We are now going to go into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, at the beginning of 1995, where was your battalion located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: My battalion was located on the following positions: to the left, Lomanac brook, the village of Pajici, Gaj, Lemesac, Stolice, Vresinje, trig 555, Ilina Bara exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher to have Defence Exhibit D25 shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, you said -- you told us what those points were. Could you take a look at the map, please. Place it in front of you, and draw into it with the marker that you will find in front of you these points, and we'll put the map back onto the ELMO once you have done that for your explanations for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, you need not place the map on the ELMO, but this will be a problem for the Trial Chamber, I fear, because we can see the markings of the other brigades. But let us try it another way. Mr. Usher, could you just place the upper portion on the ELMO? No. I think that we could overcome this problem by availing ourselves of the services of the Prosecutor. They have a map which has not been marked previously, so the witness can mark in the points on that map. Yes, Mr. Usher, you may place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could get a new number for that exhibit so we can make it clear. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Registrar, may we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number could be D25/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And perhaps we ought to clarify matters. Mr. Petrusic, once the witness has marked something into the exhibit, then the exhibit must be marked for -- that is to say, it must be corrected. We ought to know what the witness has inscribed on the exhibit in order to be able to revert back to the origin of the exhibit. Mr. Petrusic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, is that the line of your position, the one you held in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For purposes of the record, can you tell us what line that was with the places marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I spoke in more detail of some points that are not on the map, but as I was in that region of defence, I know them very well and they are the following features: The Lomanac stream inclusive, the Pajici feature. This is where the Gaj feature is, approximately. Then we have the Lemesac feature; Stolice; Vresinje; trig 555; Ilina Bara as it was called, exclusively. That is to say, there is a road here. It is a bad road, dirt road, and below that road was where my last soldier was, just underneath that dirt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For purposes of the record, the witness has, on D25/1, Exhibit D25/1, drawn in with a green marker the line which was his position in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your unit control the road from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who controlled that road, who was in control of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: The whole time, that road was controlled by the civilian police, and they set up a permanent checkpoint in the region of Konjevic Polje. From time to time, at the entrance to the town of Bratunac, they would set up a checkpoint and control this, control the movement of military conscripts; that is to say, the military police of our brigade would control that. So that I did not have orders binding me, obliging me to control the passage of goods, resources, people, along that road, communication line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in the area of responsibility -- of your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: My battalion did not hold the area of responsibility. My battalion had a defence region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, Witness DF, tell us the difference between an area of responsibility and what you call a region of defence or a defence region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: An area of responsibility is more a peacetime designation and it does not apply to the level of battalion. In defence, a battalion is assigned a defence region and a brigade a defence zone or area. Also, on the attack, the brigade is assigned an attack zone and a battalion an axis or a direction of attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, or rather, your unit have any depth of defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: My battalion did not have a deep defence region. Actually, for there to be any defence, any depth in the defence, this implies that you have companies on the front line, on regulated and fortified positions, and in the rear second line -- a second line company holding regulated or fortified positions, which, in this particular case, I did not have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can you ask him to lower his voice because we can't hear even the translation because it is so high, so loud.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour. We didn't hear you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. His voice is so loud we cannot even listen to the translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, you have heard the comment of His Honour. Though -- the equipment is highly sophisticated, so you need not worry that we will not be able to hear you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I'll try, but as an officer, I have become accustomed to speaking out loud to my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go back now to this question. How did you defend the area if you had no depth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: My battalion had a line system of defence, a linear system, which means that, along this line that I have drawn, our soldiers were deployed. First of all, because of the assignment of the battalion and because of the size of the area it was tasked to defend for according to rules in force, a battalion can defend 3 to 5 kilometres of territory, and in this area, as you can see, the line is about 10 kilometres long. So primarily because of the possibilities of combat, the battalion was forced to organise such a method of defence in which there virtually was no defence depth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason for this was the shortage of personnel, equipment, weapons, et cetera, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the main reasons, for our battalion throughout the period had to set aside a certain number of men who were deployed elsewhere throughout the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of such a drawn-out, linear defence, were there cases of incursions of enemy groups behind the lines of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, there were such examples. In fact, many. Around mid-1993, about 500 metres from my command post, an ambush was set involving the death of civilians. Also, there were frequent incursions of groups into the area of Konjevic Polje where civilians were killed, Vojin Lazic and Ikonija Lazic. Also, in the area around the Lomanac stream, sabotage groups were infiltrated so that I requested from my superior command that this area be covered with mines so as the gap should be closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now go on to July 1995. Did you and your unit at the beginning of July 1995, were you at the position we have just described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any particular developments along the defence lines held by your battalion in those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: There was evidence of frequent provocations by enemy forces using infantry weapons, particularly from the area trig 413, Cerska Kosa.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I can't hear the witness. Could the witness speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Vicac. So as I was saying, there were provocations by the enemy, using infantry weapons, from the area of trig 413.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's all right, it is in the record, but in the future, please bear in mind that you should speak into the microphone. In view of these frequent provocations that you have mentioned, did you, or rather, your command, take any steps? Did you report to your superior command about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes. In my regular and interim reports, I would brief my command about these events, and also at regular briefings at the brigade command when I would inform the commander of the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher for his assistance, please. Could you show Exhibit 404, footnote 193, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, we have here a request written by you, asking for replenishment of materiel from your superior command. Could you tell us the reasons? This is dated the 4th of July, 1995. What are the reasons for requesting the replenishment of materiel and equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: As I have said, the enemy frequently opened fire towards my battalion, which was an indication that it was planning to do something; and also on the basis of the order issued by the brigade command to raise combat readiness to the maximum level; and on the basis of available intelligence information, according to which the enemy, with the strength equivalent to one brigade, was preparing an attack, was preparing to attack my battalion; bearing all this in mind, I took all the necessary organisational and concrete steps to be ready for the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, you mentioned the raising of combat readiness to the maximum level. You were assigned this task by the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what date that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this was on the 4th of July. We received the order to raise combat readiness to hundred per cent level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, according to this request addressed by you on the 4th of July, would you say that these were customary requests of materiel and equipment? Would it fit into your regular requirements in terms of combat sets? So could you comment on it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: As my battalion was short, first of all of ammunition and also of necessary quantities of fuel, on the same day I drafted this request in writing and addressed it to the Superior Command for replenishment with, as can be seen from this request, very small quantities of ammunition, materiel, and equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, where were you on the 6th of July, the day when the attack on Srebrenica started or, rather, the beginning of the operation Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I was at my command post in the Magasici area. Actually, my observers reported that in the broader area of the 3rd Infantry Battalion, certain explosions could be heard. I called up the operations officer on duty in the brigade, asking him what was going on. His answer was that our units were carrying out an attack and that we should raise combat readiness to the maximum. Also, it was my duty to capture my own forward command post in the area of Vresinje. Before that, I issued specific orders to my subordinate officers in connection with the need to carry out resolute defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day and the days that followed the 6th of July, did you have any clashes with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or rather, the forces of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Around that time, the provocations continued with infantry weapons, and this took the form of so-called forcible reconnaissance, or reconnaissance by force, and it was clear that members of the 28th Division were taking up positions, and it was also evident that they were regrouping around the UNPROFOR checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was fire exchanged between the participants in that conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: You mean between us and members of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I said that there were provocations with infantry weapons, and it was our duty to respond if we were directly threatened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, how long did that situation last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: It went on like that until the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, did you remain in the same positions as you have described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No. In the defence region of my battalion, the brigade Chief of Staff was also present, and I received an order from him that on that day I should take up positions in the village -- around the village of Cizmici, which I did in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you moved your line, your defence line, on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, could you show us on the map, or rather, draw on the map the line indicating the positions you took up in the afternoon of the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I will do so with a dotted line, if that is all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the dotted line indicates, the dotted green line on Exhibit D25/1, Witness DF has Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. indicated the position held by his units on the 12th of July in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the positions you took up then, did you have control over the area in your rear, behind your lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly you mean. We covered that area, and we considered it clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean that there were no enemy soldiers in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit OTP 487, and as the document identifies the unit, that is, the brigade ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this regular report of your superior command, it says that during the day, enemy -- the enemy attempted a breakthrough going through your area to Tuzla and Kladanj. Witness DF, did you see or have any knowledge about the pulling out of these units? Did you have any contact with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: When taking up these positions, we did not encounter enemy forces, nor did we, that afternoon, see them at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document also says in paragraph 2 that "our" forces are clearing the enclave and preventing the breakthrough of the enemy along the mentioned axes. Could you explain this term "clearing the enclave"? What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: It means that we have to protect ourselves against possible surprises because, according to our tactics, the enemy can be expected in the depth of our territory to seek to infiltrate diversionary sabotage groups and so-called stragglers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher for OTP 464, please. And since there are technical possibilities, to prevent the identification of the unit, that this exhibit should not be made public by the ELMO because, as far as I have been informed, it is possible for the exhibit to be seen on the monitors in the courtroom but not outside by the public, so that would be my suggestion for these exhibits, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. The technical booth will not broadcast it outside. Yes, they have taken care of it. You may continue, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, on the 14th of July you received an order to carry out a search of the terrain. Can you tell us a little more about that order as your unit is actively included and specifically referred to in paragraph 1 of this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: This order was issued to me orally, and if I may explain on the map --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just comment on the order first, and then we'll give you the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: The task of my battalion was to search the terrain within the following boundaries: To the right, the junction of the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje-Jezestica road, or elevation 316 to be more precise, up to trig point 555 exclusive, Lupoglav, trig point 675, the village of Susnjari exclusive; on the left side, the Lomanac brook or stream, the village of Hranca, the village of Pale, the feature Zvijezda, trig point 906. The command post, which I had already established in the area of the village of Cizmici, was confirmed by this order, so my command post was in the village of Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, will you now draw on the map your route, though perhaps it would be advisable to do so on another copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could use another colour, that would be helpful. I'm sure green is going to start getting a bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to suggest that. Perhaps red would be better, but there doesn't seem to be any.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I am going to mark the boundaries which my battalion was to have searched the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, DF, you can comment while you're drawing this in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: It is this junction, Bratunac-Konjevic Polje-Jezestica road, and it is elevation 316, and then we have trig point 555 exclusive, the Lupoglav feature, the village of Susnjari exclusive; on the left side, Lomanac brook or stream, the village of Pale, and the feature Zvijezda. Can I draw in where I was on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, on the line that you have just drawn in and as far as I can see, it was with respect to the Vresinje feature. Would you place the date the 13th of July there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're not able to see any of this, so it doesn't have a lot of meaning for us now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're now going to see it. I think that we have this problem of protective measures because if the witness draws in what he is drawing in on the ELMO, we would be able to follow, but that's the problem. So we're now going to have to repeat it all. But never mind, Mr. Petrusic, please proceed, and let us see the reasoning of the witness. Let's follow what he's been doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness, on Exhibit D25/1, used a blue marker to draw in the line of the search of the terrain pursuant to the order received on the 14th of July, 1995, and underneath the Vresinje feature, which was also indicated with a blue marker, he wrote the date, the 13th of July, that is to say, the position that he and his unit -- where he and his unit were located on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, is that locality --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, where is the date? I don't see it. Where has the witness indicated the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes. It's not quite clear. I apologise. It's a very thick marker. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, could you write the date in with an ordinary biro so that we can see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, you and your -- that is to say, from this position where you were on the 13th of July, in the direction of Vresinje Pale, did you start clearing the terrain pursuant to order 453/2 of the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us please, Witness DF, which positions did you reach in this operation of clearing up the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: When I received the order on that day, I did not start this work because I received the order rather late in the day. So on the 14th and the 15th, from these positions, I started reconnaissance work. I did reconnoitering in front of the line attained, and I reported to my Superior Command about that. It was only on the 16th of July that I undertook the search of the terrain up to the features Lupoglav and somewhere around another feature, that is to say, the region of the Babuljice village at the Zvijezda feature. We did not mount up to the Zvijezda feature because it was rather inaccessible. It was difficult to reach. And during those days, we did not have -- we did not engage in any combat with the enemy forces. There was no fighting nor did we see the enemy at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, we have an order here from your Superior Command dated the 14th of July. I'm not going to place it on the ELMO, but the order says that: "A smaller portion of the enemy forces is still located in the Bokcin Potok-Siljkovici-Mratinjci area." Do you happen to know anything about that, although in your previous answer you said that you did not come across any enemy forces while you were clearing up the terrain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Well, during those few days, we could hear, in the region, fighting. We could hear fighting in the region, small-intensity fighting. Therefore, we assumed that the enemy was there, somewhere around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, I apologise for interrupting, but the order that you mentioned, does it have a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for reminding me. The Defence referred to exhibit -- OTP Exhibit 534, first paragraph of the order from the Superior Command of Witness DF. From Witness DF's Superior Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this would be an opportune moment to take a break, Mr. Petrusic. Yes? You agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us take a 20-minute break. The witness will remain where he is for the moment until we leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Petrusic and the witness. Would you perhaps ask him - I'm just trying to follow the testimony - if they could hear fighting in the region and he assumed that the enemy was around, I'm unclear as to who was fighting against the enemy if it wasn't his battalion. I'd just like to get that point clarified, if I could. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And another thing, Mr. Petrusic; now that we have the map on the ELMO, perhaps the witness could use his pointer to go through the lines and tell us what the lines signify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: This line here, the first line, represents the positions at which I was located until the 12th of July. This dotted green line represents the position I took up with the bulk of my forces on the 12th of July in the afternoon hours. The blue line here represents the line we reached on the 13th of July where I moved my position tactically from this position to that position, the next position; and in the region of the village of Pale, I was able to link up with the 5th Company of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And to conclude, the red line was already on the map and has nothing to do with your testimony; is that correct? Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As there are many lines, Witness DF, could you please go back to your own line, the line you occupied at the beginning of 1995. Tell us, please, what those positions were. What trig points did you hold? What were their names, the names of the places or the trig points, please. Could you give us those, and then you can comment and say that it's the blue line -- no, this is the green line. So in 1995, we're dealing with 1995, the beginning of 1995, "I was on the following -- at the following positions."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Inclusive, the Lomanac stream or brook, the Pajici feature, the Gaj feature, Lemesac, Stolice, a little behind this trig point 532 Vresinje, or at trig point 555 exclusive. That is to say, below this trig point, there's a dirt road there, and that's where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the position you held on the 6th of July as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us in the same way the positions on the 12th of July, 1995. Could you indicate those, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Let me start off from the other side. Ilina Bara, I had to leave a portion of my forces there, the equivalent of one company, and about two platoons of a second company. And with the 3rd Company and 4th and 5th Companies, I took up this position here, the region from the Vresinje feature via Cizmici up to Bljecevska River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, your positions on the 13th of July, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, I resorted to tactical movement as I was in an unfavourable position should the enemy open fire from the Pale elevation. So I moved for tactical reasons and took up the line from the Vresinje feature to the Pale feature, exclusive, where I linked up with the 2nd Infantry Battalion, as I said earlier on, and their 5th Company. I was there personally and was able to join up these forces, make the link.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, Judge Wald asked you a question, and could you answer that, please; that is to say, did you hear or were you fighting the enemy or members of the 28th Division, rather, while clearing up the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I said that we heard low-intensity fighting approximately in the region of Bokcin Potok, that area. We did not enter into combat at all or have any conflicts or clashes with the enemy side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Can I just still clarify. Then who was doing -- the enemy was fighting who? If it wasn't your battalion, who was it? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I indicated that this was outside my region, my area, so I couldn't see it. I couldn't actually see it nor could I go into action. This was done by units which I did not know. I do not know which.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher now give us OTP Exhibit 539, please, and 538 as well. OTP Exhibit 539 and 538. May we have Exhibit 539 first, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, in this daily combat report from your Superior Command sent to the Command of the Drina Corps, in paragraph 2 states, that is to say, it says that a battalion from your battalion has been set aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now have Exhibit 538, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pursuant to this order, which your Superior Command dispatched to your unit, your battalion, the whole of your battalion was set aside and pulled out for engagement towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bearing in mind these two exhibits and the two statements, assertions, made in those two orders, Witness DF, did you and your unit, on the 16th of July, go to the Zepa combat area? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Not on the 16th. I left on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the whole of your unit, your complete unit, leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, including this intervention platoon which was mentioned earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, how do you explain the fact that these two orders were issued on the same day and the difference being that in one order it is stated that the intervention platoon of your unit should be separated and in the second order it is stated that the complete battalion should be dispatched, deployed, to the Zepa region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I explained that fact by the following: In the course of those days, events followed each other rapidly, there was a rapid success of events, and that orders had to be changed and issued as the developments evolved, and they had to be adopted to the newly-arisen situation, to the developments. So also this order for me to dispatch the intervention platoon was not executed. This order was not implemented because of the importance of the second task, the second assignment, dispatching me to the general area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, finally, you mentioned at the beginning of your testimony that you received an order to put up a decisive defence. I think this was on the 6th of July. In that order or in some other documents, did you -- that is to say, did your Superior Command envisage the treatment of any possible prisoners of war? Did it provide for that in the region of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I received that order in writing on the 6th of July, and it was brought to me personally by the Chief of Staff when he came to my area. That order contained the provision that my battalion, as I stressed, should put up a resolute defence; and linked to the question of prisoners of war, it envisaged, provided for, a collection -- a holding area, a collection area at Pribicevac. That means that they did not foresee the fact that on my axis or in the -- my battalion's area, there could have been any prisoners of war. That was not ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact have any prisoners of war, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, we can note that on the 17th of July you went to engage in combat in the Zepa area. How long did you remain in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I remained in that area until approximately the 5th or 6th of August. I can't remember the exact date, but it was the beginning of August, sometime -- until sometime at the beginning of August, when I returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under whose command was your battalion at Zepa, within the operations at Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Under the direct command of my brigade commander, Colonel --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would hope that that last name will be stricken from the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that concludes my examination of this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you finished, or do you plan to finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished my examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. So, is it Mr. McCloskey? Your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could go in closed session briefly for some background questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's go into closed session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge that the Bratunac Brigade was involved in the offensive operations of Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I was aware on the basis of the order I received from my brigade commander to the effect that the brigade, with a smaller portion of its forces, should act, should participate in the offensive operations. But I underline that I received that order only on the 6th of July and that before that I had no knowledge of any such assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your assignment in participation of the attack was a resolute defence in your area of responsibility; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes. Literally, the words were "decisive defence."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in an offensive operation such as Krivaja 95, that can be referred to as a decisive defence in the context of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could we show the witness OTP Exhibit 751, but could we make sure that the ELMO is not going over the public.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you occasionally went to command meetings at the brigade command; is that right? You've got to answer out loud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could look briefly at the exhibit which you should be getting the B/C/S copy of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could put the English, the first page of the English on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could look briefly at that, especially the first part that refers to your battalion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I don't remember the details of it, but I do remember it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mention having -- suggesting problems with conscripts in town, and if you could look at the end of the document where Major Nikolic is referenced, that he agrees that conscripts and passes should be controlled, but he says there he thinks something was wrong with the battalion when so many conscripts were reported to the police. Do you remember the discussion or the exchange with Major Nikolic that you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: It was a problem that we had from earlier on, but it wasn't dramatic. There weren't that many, but a certain number of military conscripts behaved in an undisciplined manner and would arbitrarily abandon positions, and it was precisely for that reason in the aim of raising discipline to a higher level that I requested that tighter control be imposed on the movement of conscripts in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the Major Nikolic mentioned in this meeting is this Major Momir Nikolic, head of security and intelligence for the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have a security officer in your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his or her name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, that will identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Then we better go into closed session, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private session then, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time period from July 6th through July 17th when you went to Zepa, what kind of communications did you have outside your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I had communication with the Superior Command and with subordinate units, mostly with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were able to communicate with the neighbouring battalions in your area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Only when that was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you communicate with the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your brigade command have the ability to communicate with the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're in a very difficult position with potential enemy soldiers coming at you from several different sides, if I followed your testimony, and it would have been very important for you to able to communicate with all VRS units in the area, would it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: In view of my level of command and the established hierarchy in the army, all requests that do not concern my level go through the Superior Command. I did not have the obligation nor the need to directly communicate with those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where the MUP units were located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no idea whatsoever on, let's say, July 12th and July 13th where any MUP units were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the local MUP units of Bratunac and Zvornik and Milici, did they form combat companies or squads for potential assistance in combat operations to the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I think they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You think they did? As an officer in the VRS involved in a war, is that -- do you want a little more time to think about that, to answer that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: There were such units. I know that because, for example, in the area of Trnovo, I knew that there was one such unit, but this was at the end of 1995. So I assume that, in those days too, that unit was operating. But as regards its structure and anything specific about it is something I don't know because we did not participate together in any combat operation or combat activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Ljubisa Borovcanin, do you not, from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I do know Ljubisa Borovcanin from the time when he was the chief of the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of a special combat organisation from the Ministry of Interior referred to as the Special Police as it differed from the municipal police combat organisations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I've heard of it. Such units exist to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Borovcanin's position in the Special Police in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I think he was deputy commander of that brigade. I think from the position of chief of the police station, he was transferred to that position, as far as I am aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the Special Police doing, the Special Police under Borovcanin doing on July 12th, July 13th, July 14th, 1995, near your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: First of all, my battalion does not have an area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence would like to object because we feel that the Prosecutor should first ask the witness whether he knows whether that unit was located in his area of responsibility on those days and only then go on to ask his next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. McCloskey, I think you will have no problem in following the suggestion of Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think that was implicit in the question, but I can certainly make that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but it is, in a sense, leading. But in any event, I think there is no problem in asking, first, the witness whether he knew and then go on to your next question. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the Special Police was on July 12th, 13th, or 14th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn where they were during those time periods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Nothing specific, but from media reports and subsequent information. But in those days, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have no idea whatsoever that the MUP Special Police were along the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, just north of your position, during those time periods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I am convinced that they were not at all in my region, in my area, my defence area. And also when you mention north of that area, I really Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. don't know that, nor was it my duty to know that, nor did anyone from the superior command tell me anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would have been responsible for blocking enemy units infiltrating from the area of Lomanac brook into the rear of your area on July 11th, 12th, 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Specifically related to that area, battle would be fought with them by units in the immediate vicinity. And in the event of a larger-scale blockade, if that sabotage group were to escape us and we would not get into direct contact with it, I would have to seek assistance from the superior command, and then the brigade commander would decide as to who would participate in blocking that sabotage group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've stated that the area of the Lomanac brook was a common area for infiltration. Can you tell us what unit would have protected your rear on July 12th from coming into that area, or are you suggesting that after they came in and attacked, then you would call for someone to protect your rear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: If we were to identify an enemy sabotage group, then we would intervene in the way I have just described.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no unit that you're aware of that was protecting your rear from the area of Lomanac brook?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Not that I know of. And anyway, in the area, there was an unidentified minefield, and this Lomanac brook during the daytime could be relatively successfully controlled by fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, referring you back to Exhibit 751, I noticed there's the -- another person from another battalion requests an anti-aircraft machine gun. Can you tell us -- I note the Bratunac Brigade is a small unit. Can you tell us how many anti-aircraft machine guns you had at the time in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: You mean my battalion?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in the whole --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your whole brigade, and whether or not if your battalion had one also.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I did, but there were a couple, maybe four or five in the battalion. And I really don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many did you have that were actually on wheeled vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I didn't have any machine gun on a wheeled vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many anti-aircraft guns were there on wheeled vehicles in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't know that either, because I am not aware of the numbers for the whole brigade. And I wouldn't say that there were any on vehicles, any such anti-aircraft gun on wheeled vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going to the Exhibit 778. I don't know if we need to bring it up or not, but you request a certain number of items. In item number four, it's referred to - well, in the English - as petrol for a self-propelled item of some sort, the word "samohotka." What is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes. It is a samohotka of 76 millimetres of American make, a very, very old piece of equipment which used oil as fuel or petrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this have tyres on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No, no, it had tracks. It had very low capacity, a very small tank for fuel, but it consumed about 300 to 400 litres per 100 kilometres. In those days, we were short of fuel, we had a big shortage, so that it was never -- its tank was never filled to capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to Exhibit 782/A and also continue not to have that exhibited on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report from your command, and it states the Chief of Staff is in the particular area of responsibility. What was the Chief of Staff doing there on the 9th in that area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff assisted me in my work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any artillery pieces in your area, either belonging to your unit or to the brigade or to the corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: If you consider mortars as an artillery piece, I did have them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from mortars, were there anything heavier than mortars in your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I had this Samohotka, this self-propelled gun. And I don't know which calibre you consider a heavier weapon to be, from which calibre on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the Chief of Staff, in particular, helping you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: In organising the system of fire, in viewing the situation on the ground and, should a problem arise, we would deal with it together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you look -- as a military person, you're aware of different kinds of weapons and ammunition, are you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could look under paragraph 6 of this Exhibit 782/A, and we go down perhaps a little bit beyond halfway through the list and there is something listed as "Bullets, 20/3 700 pieces." What kind of ammunition is that and what is it used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: It is ammunition for an anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the "20" stands for the millimetres? That's the size of the ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, 20 millimetres, yes. And "3" stands for three barrels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so a little bit farther down the line, we have "Bullets, 30/2 200 pieces." That is 30-millimetre two-barrelled anti-aircraft gun ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can anything besides an anti-aircraft gun fire this ammunition that was in the possession of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I think that some kind of improvised weapons were made that can use such bullets. Grenade launchers. I don't know specifically for this ammunition, but these were indeed used mostly for the guns. I assume that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This kind of ammunition cannot be used for a grenade launcher, can it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: For a weapon? For an infantry weapon you mean? These are anti-aircraft weapons and ammunitions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we now go to Exhibit 752.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DF, this is -- you'll have a chance to take a look at it. These are notes from the command meeting, and there is a note at the bottom of it for 5 July, and the -- notes that the Chief of Staff will go to the particular battalion to increase the accuracy in a direction of artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the chief actually assisting you in the direction of the artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I have already said that the Chief of Staff assisted in the organisation of what we call the system of fire, which includes this more specific reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you have weapons that were capable of artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Which calibre are you interested in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any calibre of artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I had mortars, as I have said; one mortar of 60 millimetres, several 82-millimetre mortars, and I think a couple of 120 millimetres. That is all that can be placed under the heading of "Pieces." These are mostly in infantry units, and they are considered battalion fire groups, and they are of lesser range. Also, I was very short of ammunition of these calibres, extremely short of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So under your definition, a mortar could be considered an artillery weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't say that that was an artillery weapon because, according to current provisions for establishment, a mortar, especially an 82-millimetre mortar, is manned by soldiers with infantry speciality, what we called VES, V-E-S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could go now to Exhibit 753, and -- but if we could just have that ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to getting that document, could we -- can you tell me where the area of Gornji Potocari is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: If you give me a map, I can show it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just describe it? We know where the Potocari compound was, and could you first describe it, and we'll have a map also.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I can. That is where Naser Oric's house is situated, so that is how I know where it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is it in relation to the Potocari former Dutch compound that we know about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: It is -- when you go along the road to Srebrenica, I think you take a turn next to the school at Potocari and then you reach Gornji Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many kilometres is it from the DutchBat compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Approximately 4 or 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in the direction of Vlasenica, or basically west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, more or less west -- no. I really don't know. I can't tell you now, but I can show you on the map. Vlasenica is quite distant, a distance away from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could take a look at this Exhibit 753/A in the B/C/S, and if we could put the regular exhibit on the ELMO. This is a document that has as a heading, From the Command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, dated 12 July, to the Drina Corps Command, attention Major Golic. Now, you know that Major Golic was an intelligence officer in the Drina Corps command on that date, do you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I don't know. I had no dealings whatsoever with intelligence officers of higher level commands, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is authored by a Captain Pecanac, and did you have any knowledge that Captain Pecanac was a Main Staff security officer, working under Ljubo Beara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: As I was saying, I had no contact with Captain Pecanac or Major Golic or any other people from the superior command, from the intelligence or security sections, so I really cannot tell you whether that is that particular man. I don't know what positions he held. I really don't know what they were doing or what they engaged in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a Captain Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any intelligence reports about the Muslim column on the 12th of July from any source?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I don't remember explicitly, but it is possible that we were warned to -- in order to be alert and to avoid any surprises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't see -- you didn't capture one Muslim prisoner throughout this entire time period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the column at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we show the witness Exhibit 809 bis. It's the blowup.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this will be a map, and if you could take the pointer. Now, I know you've already marked -- hopefully the -- this can be put on the ELMO so Defence can see it. And the markings on it in red are only on this exhibit, but since you've already marked on a map some locations, I would just ask you to point to the area where your unit was during the July 10th, 12th, time period.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The witness is going -- I'm sorry, he's going to need the microphone, so we may need another usher, so ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Let me repeat. The Lomanac brook inclusive, the Pajici feature. This is the Gaj feature which can be seen on the map here. It's rather -- the ratio is 1:25.000. Lemesac is next, then we have the Vresinje feature a little behind the trig point here, moving towards the Ilina Bara feature and trig point 555. I said this exclusive. Below this road here, that's where my soldiers were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And this is a map that was confiscated from the Zvornik Brigade that was put together by the members of the Zvornik Brigade. And noting the large circle with the arrow attached to it, that is designed to represent the Muslim column that assembled there on the 11th of July and left in that area. From your position as you have just described, could you see members of the Muslim column fleeing in the direction of that arrow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I could see parts of the column withdrawing from the positions around here somewhere, the Pajici feature, and from the Vresinje feature moving towards Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you fire upon that column with your mortars and your other weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: As you can see, that is outside the range of the kind of weaponry that I had, so I did not open fire, no. I did not open fire on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you feel that column was a threat to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I did not consider it to be a threat to me, so I did not act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you think it was a threat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Because it wasn't jeopardising my own combat positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, may the witness be seated again?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a good idea, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that would make it more comfortable for him and for the usher as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I tried to have a setup, but with the protection, they weren't allowed to fit in the easel.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. McCloskey, if I can make a suggestion. If the witness stays seated and the usher holds the map and makes the pointer longer, then it could be shown on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I think for now we can go on to another area.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could show the witness exhibit number 95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, perhaps we could take a break at this point. I have just been informed that General Krstic is in need of a break. So let us have our 50-minute break; that is to say, we shall reconvene at around 1.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we show the witness Exhibit 95. And that can be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this is a rather unique-looking artillery piece. This is a two-barrelled 30-millimetre artillery gun; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, known as Praga. As far as I can see, this is 30/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recognise this particular vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- can you read what's been said on the side of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: "Lok" something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not a relatively infamous vehicle in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. What did you say? Which was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever read about this particular vehicle in any literature, magazines, papers, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Not for this particular vehicle, but I do know what a Praga is as a means of anti-air defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what particular village was your headquarters in prior to the Krivaja 95 operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: In concrete terms, in the village of Magasici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it particularly in the village of Bozici or in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Well, Bozici, we're a little above that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll get to a map that will help us with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can show the witness Exhibit 757.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we're getting there, did you receive any information at that time, any time, that the VRS killed thousands of Muslim prisoners from the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of any information that's credible from Serbian sources that thousands of Muslims were killed between July 13th and July 19th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Only after the war in the information media, the mass media, did these cases begin to be talked about, and it was only then that I could have heard or learnt something more about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard not one word from any VRS source at all about what occurred between the 13th of July, 1995 and the 19th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that thousands of Muslim prisoners were taken along the Bratunac-Milici road in the areas of Konjevic Polje-Nova Kasaba-Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: As I say, only after the war, from the information media, but that I saw anything or knew anything, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could look at this map and take a pen and if you could mark in a small circle, if you could, the area where your headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how -- after July 12th, did your headquarters remain in that position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No. As I said earlier on, together with me -- that is to say, first of all, the forward command post, on the 6th of July, was established, and after the 12th, the officers, the superior officers of my battalion went, and then the command post was where I was, which means in the area of the Cizmici village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did your headquarters actually move from the particular spot you've marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Well, most of the command at the 6th was already at the forward command post, but together with me on the 12th there were my officers too. We went, the command post and everything else that that implies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we hold up just very briefly this large Exhibit 809 bis again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've discussed the order that you received on the 14th to search the area, and is it not correct that the northernmost boundary of the area you searched was between the points of 1 and 5 on the map, I think 5 being the area of Lomanac brook and 1 being the area of Jezestica road junction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: That's this region here. This is the brook towards the village of Pale, and then we have this part here towards the Lupoglav feature. Pale-Lupoglav, that is the axis. But I did not return, I kept going forward. I did not have the obligation to see what was happening behind me or going back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your area of search was that V-shaped area between the numbers that have been marked 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Well, that's roughly so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the northernmost boundary of your search area was the Bratunac-Milici road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I had nothing to do with that road. I went off from the lines attained. What you're saying now is this here. It's a zone, an area, that is to say, a direction, an axis in which I would move. Now, for that axis to be denoted, you have to denote it for several points, and I had absolutely no goings back. There was no logic in going back and, therefore, relinquishing my positions to the enemy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness, could you please speak a little bit softer. We can't hear the interpretation here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I have this deep, strong voice, and I am accustomed, as I said, to speaking loudly. Pity I'm not an opera singer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the area between point 1, Jezestica road, and point 5, the Lomanac brook, if you draw -- can you just take a pointer and draw a line between the two, just an imaginary line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that area between the imaginary line between point 1 and point 6 north to the roadway, was that searched by your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you received your orders to search to the right of Jezestica road over to Lomanac brook, you did not go up at all to that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. roadway; that was an area left completely unreconned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Let me try again. Let me repeat this. I did not have any need or obligation to go back, to go backwards and to search something that is to the back of me, my rear; nor was I supposed to do that, because that would have left me open to allowing the enemy to take over the positions I had already gained control of. So it is from the lines attained, reached, that we went forwards, not backwards. Never backwards, just forwards. And that is standard practice, that's what you're supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So have you seen the video of the soldiers all along that road in that area with their guns pointing up towards the direction where you would have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think so. If you have them, perhaps I can take a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't concerned that there may be Muslims in that large area that you were -- between you and the road that was not being searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: During those days, many moved along that road, a lot of things were going along that road, both the refugees, Muslims that were being transported from the Potocari region. So there was a lot of coming and going, a passage of people, movement of people, and so I did not consider it to be necessary to do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did receive --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Nor did I receive any orders to do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did receive information that people were going along that roadway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Not in that way. I assumed that that was being done. Not that somebody directly informed me how much, what, for what reason, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or any of your recon units or any of your men have the possibility to see that road on July 13th or 14th to see what was going on on that road on those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Well, from these positions, they could just observe movement. They could just observe movement, the means that were passing along that way, but nobody informed me about any activities which would influence the establishment of a defence system, and, therefore, it was not the subject of my interests. I did not focus on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did have information from your soldiers who could see from the heights down on top of that road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes, they could see, but they did not inform me of any specifics with respect to that, and they were at a great distance. They were very far off, approximately 3 kilometres as the crow flies. That's where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they inform you that units along that road were firing heavy weapons up in the direction of where they would have been watching from, all along the road from Konjevic Polje down to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 758.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness DF, you'll recognise -- this is a blow-up of one of the previous maps, and this is a NATO map. This is not the VRS map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you again mark on this blow-up, so we get a little better idea, where your headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DF
utterances.text: I can't do that on this map because it's not in the framework of the map, as far as I can see. I can show you on the other map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
